paper.title: Advancing extrapolative predictions of material properties through learning to learn using extrapolative episodic training
paper.research_summary: This study develops a meta-learning methodology—extrapolative episodic training (E2T)—to enhance machine learning models' ability to predict material properties beyond the distribution of training data. Using attention-based matching neural networks (MNNs) trained on arbitrarily generated extrapolative tasks, the approach demonstrates superior generalization for unseen material domains, validated on two case studies: predicting specific heat and refractive index of polymeric materials, and bandgap of hybrid organic–inorganic perovskites.

tasks.objective: To develop a machine-learning methodology that enables extrapolative (not just interpolative) prediction of physical properties for materials outside the training data distribution.
constraints: need to predict beyond boundaries of existing data
models must generalize to unexplored material spaces
input_requirements: material composition and structural features encoded as descriptors (e.g., Morgan fingerprint for polymers, crystal structure for perovskites)
output_goal: real-valued physical property prediction (y ∈ ℝ) for unseen material domains

evidence.text: Central to this progress is the development of rapidly computable property predictors, which allow identifying novel materials with the desired properties from vast material spaces.

The most signiﬁcant challenge in data-driven materials research is the scarcity of data resources... the ultimate goal of materials science is to discover “innovative” materials from an unexplored material space. However, machine-learning predictors are generally interpolative and their predictability is limited to the neighboring domain of the training data.

In this study, we leveraged the attention-based architecture of neural networks and a meta-learning algorithm to enhance extrapolative generalization capabilities. Meta-learners trained repeatedly on arbitrarily generated extrapolative tasks show outstanding generalization for unexplored material spaces.

stages.stage_name_raw: acquisition of polymer and perovskite datasets
stages.stage_goal: To obtain computational material property datasets for training and evaluation.
stage_output: 69,480 amorphous polymers with Cp and refractive index

evidence.text: In the polymer-property prediction experiments, 69,480 samples of Cp and 68,700 samples of the refractive index were used for the amorphous homopolymers. The data were generated using RadonPy36, which is a Python tool to construct a workﬂow for fully automated calculations of various polymeric properties using all-atom MD simulations.
The HOIP dataset40,41 contains 1345 perovskite compounds and their properties, including bandgaps, dielectric constants, and relative energies, calculated using the density functional theory.

stages.stage_goal: To encode material structures into fixed-dimensional numerical representations suitable for model input.
stage_input: chemical structure of polymer repeating unit

evidence.text: The chemical structure of a polymer repeating unit was encoded through Morgan ﬁngerprinting38,39 into a 2048-dimensionaldescriptor vector, which served as the input for a three-layer fullyconnected neural network (FCNN) employed as the embedding function ϕ of MNN.

The count-based Morgan ﬁngerprint38, a type of extended connectivity ﬁngerprint (ECFP)39, was utilized as a descriptor for the repeating unit of a homopolymer. The descriptor was calculated using RDKit55, with a radius of 3 and bit length of 2048.

The MPNN44 was employed as the encoder for the crystal structures in all models. The MPNN architecture was designed in a manner similar to that proposed by Na and Park42, with an embedding size of 32.

stages.stage_goal: To construct training episodes where test instances (x, y) lie outside the support set S’s domain, enabling extrapolative learning.
stage_input: partitioning strategy by polymer class or cation/anion combinations
stage_output: episodes (xi, yi, Si) with extrapolative relationships

evidence.text: Numerous episodes were generated from a given dataset D, each comprising a training set S and test set Q containing instances outside the training domain S.
For a given dataset, we can generate a set of episodes for extrapolative learning with ﬂexible quantity and quality. This is considered a type of self-supervised learning.

In each step of E2T, a training instance on (x, y) was sampled from a randomly selected polymer class, whereas the support set S was entirely sampled from the 19 polymer classes, including interpolative and extrapolative episodes.

We classiﬁed the HOIP dataset into 12 categories (or domains) based on a combination of four inorganic anions and three cations. Data from 11 of the 12 categories were included in the training dataset D. To evaluate the model performance, 10% of the data in D were used for validation. In each step of E2T, a training instance at (x, y) was sampled from a randomly selected combination among the 11 anion–cation combinations, whereas the support set S with a size of m = 50 was sampled from the remaining ten combinations of anions and cations, resulting in the inclusion of only extrapolative episodes.

stages.stage_name_raw: meta-training of matching neural networks via extrapolative episodic training (E2T)
stages.stage_goal: To train attention-based MNNs to learn the mapping y = f(x, S) across diverse extrapolative episodes.

evidence.text: We employed a meta-learning algorithm30–34, commonly known as “learning to learn,” to impart extrapolative prediction capabilities to the MNNs.
E2T learning is formulated as ℓ2 loss minimization as follows: Jϕ = Σ(yi − f(xi, Si))²
Training of MNNs by E2T. The attention-based model, which resembles the kernel ridge regressor in Eq. (2), was implemented in PyTorch56.

stages.stage_goal: To assess generalization to unseen material domains by testing on held-out classes or element combinations.
stage_output: RMSE and R² scores for extrapolative prediction

evidence.text: To evaluate the prediction performance for an unseen polymer class, the following process was implemented: (1) a model was trained using randomly selected samples from 19 of the 20 polymer classes and (2) its generalizability was assessed using data from the remaining polymer class.

We performed numerical experiments using the same setting as that employed by Na et al.42,43. The HOIP dataset was divided into 12 groups based on the combinations of four anions and three cations. For creating a training episode, we excluded all samples with Ge and F or with Pb and I and randomly selected 50 instances of (x, y) from one group while drawing S of size 50 from the 10 remaining groups.

stages.stage_goal: To adapt pretrained meta-learners to target domains with limited data, evaluating transferability and rapid adaptation.
stage_output: fine-tuned predictor optimized for target domain

evidence.text: Fine-tuning was performed on the RadonPy dataset. In this experiment, a pretrained E2T model with a source data size of 38,000 was ﬁne-tuned on data from the target domain corresponding to a particular polymer class.
An MNN pretrained by E2T with a source data size of 1248 (HOIP-GeF) or 1228 (HOIP-PbI) was ﬁne-tuned on data, including data from the target domain.
